messages:
sophia: Quick RFC follow-up — we need to finalize the minimal runtime-adapter handshake.

sophia: Problem: hosted, dedicated, private adapters diverge in auth, telemetry, and capability exposure. We should define a compact capability vector and an extensible negotiation.

raj: +1. Can we avoid per-request capability negotiation? prefer a once-on-connect capability announce and per-request fallback flags.

miguel: Agreed. Proposal: on connect adapter sends `capabilities` list + `protocol_version`. Something like:
```
capabilities:
  - kvcache
  - streaming
  - quantized_int8
protocol_version: v1beta2
```

jess: What about auth? Private adapters will use KMS + mTLS, hosted uses API keys. Need map of auth modes so control plane can route without leaking tokens.

sophia: Right — add `auth_modes` to the handshake. Control plane keeps auth tokens out of the handshake, only mode names.

oliver: Telemetry/metrics — dedicated adapters may not want full token-level traces. Add `telemetry_level` enum: none/minimal/full.

infra-bot: deploy: adapter-protocol v1beta2 accepted on prod clusters :white_check_mark:

raj: Also call out semantics for fallbacks: adapter must advertise compatible model variants (e.g., float32 vs quantized). E.g. `variants: ["gptx-30b-fp16","gptx-30b-int8"]`

miguel: Implementation note: keep handshake tiny (<1KB) to avoid adding latency on warm connections. Use protobuf or compact json.

jess: Ops ask: please document error codes for capability mismatch so we can give actionable errors to customers.

sophia: Action items:
- raj to draft capability schema + error codes (deadline: 48h)
- miguel to prototype protobuf wire format
- jess to document auth-modes and telemetry levels for SOC review

sophia: If no objections I'll fold this into the RFC update and submit by EOW.

oliver: No objections from infra, thumbs up.

raj: will start the draft now.

sophia: thanks everyone :pray:
